title: Branzino al Forno
subtitle: Italian oven-baked sea bass with lemon and herbs
excerpt: Whole sea bass baked simply with lemon, garlic and rosemary. The skin crisps, the flesh stays moist and the fish absorbs the Mediterranean aromatics as it cooks. This needs nothing more than good olive oil and a glass of white wine alongside.
sourceNotes: Branzino (sea bass) is the most popular fish in Italian coastal cooking. Baked whole in the oven with lemon, herbs and olive oil is the most common way to cook it -- simple enough to let the fish speak for itself.

content.text: Score the skin before baking. Three diagonal cuts on each side allow the heat to reach the flesh faster and let the flavour from the cavity travel through. The fish is done when the flesh flakes easily at the thickest point.

items.prepNote: about 600g each, gutted and scaled -- or 4 sea bass fillets if whole fish unavailable
half sliced for the cavity, half for squeezing over
2 sliced thin for the cavity, 1 crushed for rubbing over the skin

content.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Pat the fish dry inside and out with kitchen paper.
Score each fish with 3 diagonal slits on each side, cutting about 1cm deep into the flesh.
Season the inside of each fish with salt. Stuff the cavity with the lemon slices, rosemary and sliced garlic.
Rub the outside of each fish with crushed garlic, olive oil and plenty of salt. Place in a roasting tin.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, depending on the size of the fish. The flesh should flake easily when pressed at the thickest point behind the head.
Rest for 5 minutes. Squeeze lemon over the top. Drizzle with more olive oil. Serve directly from the tin.

items.symptom: Fish skin sticks to the tin
items.cause: Tin not oiled, or fish too wet before going in
items.fix: Always oil the roasting tin and pat the fish dry. A preheated tin also helps prevent sticking.
Check the fish 5 minutes early. A 600g sea bass needs about 20 minutes. Thinner fish cook faster. Test by pressing at the thickest point -- it should flake when pressed.

content.text: Sea bass is the great fish of the Italian Mediterranean coastline. It is eaten from Sicily to Liguria. The simplest preparation is always the best. Good olive oil makes the dish.
